title: 清平乐·村居
titleEn: To the Tune “Clear, Calm Music”: Village Life
author: 辛弃疾
intro: A little snapshot of one farming family: an old couple chatting a bit tipsily, two sons at work, and the youngest lying by the stream peeling lotus pods instead of helping.
analysis: 这首词像一幅农家生活的小画。上阕先写环境：低矮的茅草屋，小溪边长满青草。接着听到有人用柔和的吴地口音说话，带着几分醉意，互相逗乐，原来是一对白发的老公公和老婆婆，感情很好。下阕写三个儿子：大儿子在溪东的豆地里锄草，二儿子正在编鸡笼，最可爱的是小儿子，什么活也不干，趴在溪边剥莲蓬吃。“亡赖”就是“无赖”，这里不是骂人，而是说他调皮、淘气，词人用的是喜爱的语气。全词没有一个难懂的词，像白描一样，只写人物在做什么，一家人的勤劳、和睦和快乐却都在里面了。辛弃疾晚年闲居乡下，这首词写出了他对平静生活的喜爱。
analysisEn: This lyric is a small painting of a farming family. The first half sets the scene: a low thatched cottage, green grass along a stream. Then voices — soft southern Wu dialect, a little tipsy, teasing each other affectionately — and we see who is talking: a white-haired old man and his wife, still sweet to each other after all these years. The second half introduces their three sons. The eldest is hoeing the bean field east of the stream; the middle one is busy weaving a chicken coop. And the one the poet likes best? The youngest, a little rascal, who does no work at all — he lies on his tummy by the water peeling lotus pods to eat the seeds. The word 亡赖 (“good-for-nothing”) sounds like a scolding, but here it is said with a smile, the way a grandparent calls a child “you little monkey”. There is nothing difficult in the language: the poet simply shows each person doing one thing, and the family’s hard work, warmth and happiness come through by themselves. Xin Qiji wrote it while living in the countryside in his later years, and you can feel how much he enjoyed this quiet life.
background: Xin Qiji (1140–1207), a soldier-poet who longed to win back northern China, was dismissed from office in 1181 and spent years living at Daihu near Shangrao in Jiangxi. This lyric is usually dated to that period of village life.
pronunciation: 词牌“清平乐”的“乐”读 yuè。翁媪 wēng ǎo；亡赖 wú lài（“亡”通“无”，不读 wáng）；剥莲蓬 bāo lián peng（“蓬”在“莲蓬”里口语读轻声，本页逐字注 péng）；相媚好 xiāng mèi hǎo。机器朗读“亡”“媪”“剥”易错，已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字。
version: 采用统编小学语文教材文本。全词上下两阕，共八句。“最喜小儿亡赖”有的版本作“最喜小儿无赖”，意思相同。

lines.en: A thatched roof, low and small,

lines.lit: by the stream, green green grass.
lines.en: green grass growing by the stream.

lines.py: zuì lǐ wú yīn xiāng mèi hǎo
lines.lit: Tipsy, in soft Wu voices, they charm each other —
lines.en: Soft local voices, a little tipsy, teasing each other sweetly —

lines.py: bái fà shuí jiā wēng ǎo
lines.lit: white-haired — whose old man and old woman?
lines.en: whose white-haired old couple is this?

lines.py: dà ér chú dòu xī dōng
lines.lit: The eldest son hoes beans east of the stream;
lines.en: The eldest son hoes the beans across the stream,

lines.py: zhōng ér zhèng zhī jī lóng
lines.lit: the middle son is weaving a chicken coop.
lines.en: the middle son is weaving a chicken coop,

lines.py: zuì xǐ xiǎo ér wú lài
lines.lit: Most delightful, the youngest son, the rascal,
lines.en: and best of all, the little rascal,

lines.py: xī tóu wò bāo lián péng
lines.lit: lying by the stream, peeling lotus pods.
lines.en: lies by the water peeling lotus pods.

words.note: 茅：茅草。这里代指茅草屋。

words.en: the Wu dialect (soft speech of the lower Yangtze)
words.note: 吴：今江苏、浙江、江西东北一带。现代汉语说“吴语”。

words.en: to be sweet to each other; to tease affectionately
words.note: 媚：讨人喜欢。今天“媚”多含贬义，这里没有。
翁：老头儿；媪：老婆婆。现代汉语说“老大爷、老奶奶”。

words.en: to hoe (weeds in) the bean field

words.note: 现代汉语说“编”，如“编鸡笼”；“织”多用于布、毛衣。
亡：通“无”。今天“无赖”是骂人的话，这里是亲昵的“淘气”。
现代汉语说“躺”“趴”；“卧室”的“卧”。
现代汉语仍说，里面的莲子可以生吃。

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: 溪边青青的草写出农村清新、安静的环境。
imagery.en: Green grass by the stream sets a fresh, peaceful country scene.

imagery.name: 白发
imagery.zh: 白发老夫妻还互相逗乐，写出晚年生活的温馨。
imagery.en: An old white-haired couple still teasing each other — a warm picture of growing old together.

imagery.name: 莲
imagery.zh: 小儿子剥莲蓬，写出孩子的天真和夏天乡村的趣味。
imagery.en: The boy peeling lotus pods shows childhood innocence and the small joys of a summer village.
